Closes APRV-392.

Carter noticed at the 2026-09-19 rehearsal that the page served by
`examples/web-agent-demo/server.mjs` draws its own `approval.md` header
rather than the mark under `brand/`. That page is what a room looks at,
so it now carries `brand/wordmark.svg` itself.

## What changed

- `examples/web-agent-demo/public/index.html`: the header is
  `brand/wordmark.svg`, inlined byte for byte (spliced by script, not
  retyped), plus the `h1` rules that size it. Nothing else on the page
  moved: the four panels and the verify badge are untouched.
- `tests/demo-wordmark.test.ts`: four new tests, described below.
- `rsi/index.html` and `index.html`: **unchanged**. Both already draw the
  same two bracket paths, the same tick and the same `#17A15E`, with the
  letters set in the page's own font (and `/ rsi` hung off the end on the
  rsi page). What changes for them is that the geometry is now pinned
  instead of merely matching.

## Why inlined rather than a file in public/

Both shapes were open under AC1. The deciding argument is the security
contract at the top of `server.mjs`: it forbids a CDN and an external
font because this page is projected behind a tunnel, sometimes on a
room's network and sometimes on none at all. A header that costs a
second request is a header that can be missing in front of an audience.
Inlining also leaves that file's route table exactly as it was (it still
serves exactly one path), which is worth more than a header, because
every route on that server is part of a security argument.

## Sizing, in case it looks odd in the diff

The asset draws 176-unit type inside a 1560x320 box and carries its own
paper margin on four sides, so the CSS sizes the **box**: `--mark` at
`clamp(56px, 9vw, 88px)`, where 88px of box puts the letters at the 48px
the old `h1` used. The box is filled `#F6F3EC`, which is this page's
`--paper` to the byte, so three of those margins are invisible. The
fourth is not: 72/1560 of the width sits to the left of the "a", and a
negative margin of 72/320 of the box height pulls it back so the mark
starts on the same left edge as the badge and the panels. The right
margin is deliberately **not** pulled back, because where `.md` ends
depends on the resolved monospace font and a negative margin there could
overlap the meta line.

## Guest mode

Guest mode is an instance (`--instance guest`, its own gate directory,
its own empty vault), not a second front end: the server is handed a
`--dir` and serves this one file whichever instance that is. So "the
guest-mode variant uses the same mark" is a property of `public/` holding
exactly one page, and the test pins that, so a second front end cannot
appear without a mark check of its own.

## What the test pins

1. The `<svg>` in the demo page is `brand/wordmark.svg` verbatim. A
   copied asset is an asset that drifts.
2. The page carries no external `src`/`href`, no `@import` and no
   stylesheet or preconnect link, so it renders offline.
3. `examples/web-agent-demo/public/` holds exactly one page.
4. `index.html` and `rsi/index.html` contain the asset's two bracket
   paths, its tick path and its green, verbatim.

## Verification

- `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`: all exit 0.
- `npm test`: 4841 tests, 4818 pass, **22 fail, exit 1**. Every failure is
  the pre-existing local Node v26 SMTP class (`adapter-email`,
  `smtp-probe`, `cli-setup`'s email probes) and they share one root
  cause: Node 26 refuses a TLS `servername` set to an IP, so the tests'
  loopback SMTP servers on `127.0.0.1` cannot handshake. This lane ran on
  Node v26.8.2; **CI on Node 22 is the truth** for this PR.
- Rendered against a local static server and compared side by side with
  `/rsi`: the mark matches, it sits on the same left edge as the badge
  and the panels, and the four panels and the verify badge are unchanged.
- The browser network panel on the loaded page shows only its own
  same-origin `/api/*` polls: the header costs no request.
